author: @gittrend.io
summary: A benchmark, not a production website cloner: given a production website an agent may explore only through a browser, the agent must reverse-engineer a full-stack rebuild matching appearance and behaviour. A task passes only when functional checks pass AND every visual checkpoint reaches flat-baseline-normalised RGB SSIM 0.99. 70 websites, ~46.9k hidden test cases (post frame: 46,910; Hugging Face dataset card: 46,916 - use 46,916). Runs on the Harbor framework; each task requests 8 CPUs, 8 GiB RAM, 20 GiB disk. Plugs into agent fleet infrastructure, Kit/client work and GSE front-end as a ready-made exam and scoreboard for web agents (the job Craft Anything and fleet web agents claim to do). Risks: Apache-2.0 for benchmark code/tasks/verifier, but reference websites are third-party content, non-commercial research only; heavy per-task resources; very new (released Nov 5, 2026). First test: install the PyPI package, download one medium task, run one existing fleet agent through Harbor, record pass/fail + token cost.
metrics_or_datasets: WebsiteBench: 70 websites, 46,916 hidden test cases, visual checkpoint threshold SSIM 0.99
engine_training_value: none for the prediction engine directly - context only for the fleet. Indirect: its hidden-test + visual-SSIM labelling scheme is a labelling pattern the engine's own evaluation harness can copy (label = pass/fail per checkpoint, data lives in the task definitions on HF/GitHub).
provenance: Poster @gittrend.io is the recreator/curator; TIGER-AI-Lab is the origin. GitHub repo and Hugging Face dataset card checked this run; comment gate for the repo link NOT engaged (read-only), repo was visible in the video frame.

author: @voxaris_ai
summary: VERIFIED this run: microsoft/TokenEconomizer, arXiv 2610.22732 (Li et al., UC Berkeley / Microsoft Research / Microsoft Security), Apache-2.0, no API key of its own. An external black-box controller for coding agents with three levers: inject operational micro-skills, prune persistently irrelevant tools, intervene in unproductive failure loops. Measured (authors' own, net of controller cost): 18.4-30.9% lower mean token cost on 277 SWE-Bench tasks across 5 agent-model setups (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI; Pass@1 up in 4 of 5), 16-21% on Web-Bench, 6-20% on security-audit benchmarks. Plugins ship for Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and Pi, experimental support incl. opencode / Cursor / Hermes Agent. Caveats from the paper itself: warm-up - most repos cost MORE until about the sixth task; gains depend on repeated work in the same repo; released plugin defaults differ from the paper setup (micro-skills off by default). Plugs into agent fleet infrastructure / model-routing stack: a direct cost cut on the fleet's heaviest spend (coding-agent tokens on Beexly/Sports, a repo the fleet works repeatedly). First test: install the Claude Code plugin on one fleet seat, run 10 comparable Sports tasks with/without, compare net cost + pass rate.
metrics_or_datasets: TokenEconomizer: 18.4-30.9% lower mean token cost on 277 SWE-Bench tasks across 5 agent-model setups (authors' figures, net of controller cost)
provenance: Post by @voxaris_ai; origin is microsoft/TokenEconomizer on GitHub and the arXiv 2610.22732 paper, verified this run.
